mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 5% over the prior quarter is interpreted by market participants as a signal of tightening financial conditions, which compresses equity discount rates and reduces expected future cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.25 percentage points over the past quarter
regime_hint: early stage of a tightening cycle
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) despite the FEDFUNDS increase, or the rate rise is not sustained beyond the quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) suggests a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 10% in a month while UNRATE decreases by at least 0.2 percentage points
failure_condition: No significant correlation between PAYEMS and UNRATE changes and S&P 500 60-day forward returns, or SPX returns are negative despite the labor indicators improving.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% for three consecutive months indicates accelerating economic demand, which anticipates a rebound in consumer and business activity and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO does not show a statistically significant upward acceleration (Granger causality p > 0.05), or 5-day forward returns are not higher than the prior month's average.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the ratio of import prices (CPIAUCSL) to GDP deflator (not in catalog, so use CPIAUCSL alone) over the past month suggests softer inflation pressures, prompting the Federal Reserve to hold rates steady and allowing equity discount rates to remain low, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases by more than 0.5% month-over-month
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL does not show cooling or SPX 20-day returns are negative despite the CPIAUCSL decline.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate remains persistently below 4% in a non-recessionary regime, it signals accommodative monetary policy that lowers real interest rates, increasing the present value of expected corporate profits and pushing S&P 500 forward returns to be positive over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS rises above 4% and 20-day returns turn negative.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in job openings (PAYEMS) without a corresponding rise in layoffs indicates a labor market imbalance favoring employers, which can lead to wage growth and corporate optimism, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 20% in a single month
failure_condition: PAYEMS does not spike or SPX 60-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising retail sales (not in catalog - so use HOUST as proxy for demand) exceeding 2% growth each month suggests robust consumer demand, which elevates earnings expectations and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: HOUST does not show consistent monthly growth above 2% or SPX 20-day returns are flat or negative.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the ratio of import prices to CPIAUCSL (using CPIAUCSL as proxy) accompanied by rising industrial production (INDPRO) indicates supply-side constraints, raising uncertainty and compressing equity valuations, which tends to produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases by 1% while INDPRO increases by 3% in the same month
failure_condition: No significant negative relationship between CPIAUCSL decline and SPX 20-day returns, or INDPRO decline instead of rise.
